hot100.title: Tate McRae’s ‘Housewife’ Claims a Fourth Week at No. 1 as Michael Medrano Crashes the Top 10
hot100.subtitle: McRae's uninterrupted lead continues, while “F★CK F★REVER” surges 21 places as INTERNATIONAL MALE arrives atop albums.
hot100.text:
Tate McRae has turned an impressive debut into a sustained run at the top of the Daegon 100. “Housewife” holds at No. 1 on the chart dated November 14, marking its fourth consecutive week at the summit. Four weeks into its chart history, the song has yet to appear anywhere else: each of its four listed weeks has been spent at No. 1.

The competition directly behind McRae remains formidable. Ariana Grande's “hate that i made you love me” stays at No. 2, now in its 24th chart week and with 13 weeks at No. 1 to its name. Another Grande track, “kiss me,” climbs from No. 4 to No. 3. Jão's “Aurora” rises two positions to No. 4, matching neither its previous peak of No. 3 nor the chart's top spot, but returning to the immediate conversation around the leaders.

This week's real jolt comes at No. 9. Michael Medrano's “F★CK F★REVER” leaps from No. 30, reaching the top 10 for the first time in its 16th week on the chart. The gain coincides with the arrival of his album INTERNATIONAL MALE at No. 1 on Top 100 Albums, and its title track enters the Daegon 100 at No. 18. The simultaneous movement across songs and albums makes Medrano's breakthrough the edition's clearest new story.

Tame Impala's “Dracula (with JENNIE),” meanwhile, eases from No. 3 to No. 5 after attaining that peak the previous week. With established favorites holding close and Medrano building momentum, “Housewife” continues to lead a top 10 whose challengers are changing even as its No. 1 stays the same.

hot100.title: Tate McRae’s ‘Housewife’ Holds No. 1 for a Third Week as Tame Impala Surges Into the Top Three
hot100.text:
Three weeks into its Daegon 100 run, Tate McRae’s “Housewife” has yet to relinquish the top position. The song holds at No. 1 on the chart dated November 7, extending its opening streak to three weeks. It is an unusually uninterrupted start: the track has spent every week of its chart life at the summit.

The clearest challenge this week comes from outside the familiar top two. Ariana Grande’s “hate that i made you love me” remains at No. 2, but Tame Impala’s “Dracula (with JENNIE)” climbs from No. 15 to No. 3. That 12-place gain is the track’s highest position across its six weeks on the chart, putting it directly behind two songs that have already established considerable staying power. Grande’s single, for example, reaches its 23rd chart week, with 13 previous weeks at No. 1.

The top 10 is otherwise marked by resilience as much as movement. Grande places two additional tracks from petal at Nos. 4 and 5, while Jão holds two songs inside the top seven. Taylor Swift’s “The Fate of Ophelia,” which has previously logged six weeks atop the chart, slides one place to No. 8 in its 48th chart week. The persistence of those older hits makes Tame Impala’s advance especially notable.

For McRae, the immediate story is straightforward: “Housewife” has kept its lead even as established favorites and a rapidly climbing challenger fill out the upper ranks. Whether its reign continues will depend on the next edition, but this week’s position already gives the song a clean three-for-three opening at No. 1.
hot100.subtitle: The rising single stretches its perfect start, while Tame Impala and JENNIE deliver the week’s sharpest top-three climb.

top100Albums.title: Michael Medrano’s ‘INTERNATIONAL MALE’ Debuts at No. 1, Ending Ariana Grande’s ‘petal’ Run
top100Albums.subtitle: The new arrival opens with 107,000 units, while Grande moves to No. 2 after 11 weeks on top.
top100Albums.text:
A new album has finally dislodged Ariana Grande's petal from the summit of Daegon Top 100 Albums. Michael Medrano's INTERNATIONAL MALE debuts at No. 1 on the chart dated November 14, arriving with 107,000 units and immediately establishing a new career high on the albums ranking.

The debut breaks a major stretch of leadership for Grande. petal drops to No. 2 in its 15th chart week, having spent 11 weeks at No. 1. It adds 52,500 units this week, lifting its cumulative total in the Daegon archive to 3,889,500. The contrast is what gives Medrano's opening its weight: a first-week arrival takes the lead from an album that had made the top spot its own for much of its chart run.

Medrano's showing extends beyond the album itself. “F★CK F★REVER,” from INTERNATIONAL MALE, rises 21 places to No. 9 on the Daegon 100, a new peak in its 16th chart week. The album's title song also makes a first appearance on the songs chart at No. 18. On the Artist 50, Medrano moves from No. 15 to No. 3. Rather than a single isolated debut, the week reveals a coordinated rise across all three flagship rankings.

There is movement throughout the album chart's top tier. Jão's Memórias Póstumas climbs from No. 5 to No. 3, Anitta's EQUILIBRIVM II reaches a new No. 5 peak, and Olivia Dean's The Art of Loving leaps from No. 47 to No. 8. Yet none alters the headline: INTERNATIONAL MALE has arrived at the top, bringing an end to petal's hold on No. 1 and reshaping the chart's immediate hierarchy.

top100Albums.title: Ariana Grande’s ‘petal’ Extends Its Albums Reign to 11 Weeks While Tame Impala Makes a Major Leap
top100Albums.text:
Ariana Grande’s petal remains the album to beat on the Daegon Top 100 Albums chart dated November 7. In its 14th week on the ranking, the set collects an 11th week at No. 1, maintaining a dominant run in which the top spot has been its most familiar address.

The numbers underline the scale of that run without telling the whole story. petal earns 71,000 units for the chart week and reaches 3,837,000 total units in the Daegon archive. Yet the more revealing contrast lies immediately below it: Olivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love rises from No. 3 to No. 2 in its 21st week. Rodrigo’s album previously spent three weeks at No. 1 and now returns to the runner-up position while Grande continues to lead.

The week’s sharpest top-tier momentum belongs to Tame Impala. Deadbeat rockets from No. 23 to No. 3, a new peak in its 10th chart week. Its rise is mirrored on the Daegon 100 Songs chart, where “Dracula (with JENNIE)” advances from No. 15 to No. 3. The parallel gains make Tame Impala one of the chart week’s defining developments across formats, rather than merely an isolated albums-chart climber.

Elsewhere, Anitta’s EQUILIBRIVM II leaps from No. 28 to No. 6, and Yseult’s Freak arrives at No. 7. Those entries provide the chart with a fresh set of challengers, but for now petal continues to anchor the ranking, stretching an already substantial No. 1 total while the competition beneath it changes shape.
top100Albums.subtitle: Grande extends a lengthy No. 1 run as Olivia Rodrigo moves up and Tame Impala’s Deadbeat reaches a new high.

artists.title: Ariana Grande Reaches 130 Weeks at No. 1 on Artist 50 as Michael Medrano Hits a New Peak
artists.subtitle: Grande keeps her long-running lead, while Medrano jumps 12 spots following INTERNATIONAL MALE’s No. 1 album debut.
artists.text:
Ariana Grande holds the top position on the Daegon Artist 50 for another week, extending her cumulative total to 130 weeks at No. 1. The chart dated November 14 also marks her 475th week on the ranking, a remarkable record of longevity in an archive that dates back to June 2017.

That continuing leadership arrives during a week when her albums and songs show different patterns. Grande's petal falls from No. 1 to No. 2 on Top 100 Albums after 11 weeks at the summit, but its tracks remain prominent on the Daegon 100: “hate that i made you love me” stays at No. 2 and “kiss me” rises to No. 3. Those placements underline how a change of leader on one ranking need not mean the artist's broader presence has faded.

The most consequential new development on the Artist 50 comes from Michael Medrano, who surges from No. 15 to No. 3 in his 12th chart week. It is his best position yet, accompanying a No. 1 entry for INTERNATIONAL MALE on the albums chart. The song “F★CK F★REVER” also climbs from No. 30 to No. 9, while the album's title track debuts at No. 18. Medrano's movements across the three main charts create the week's clearest picture of an artist gaining ground on several fronts at once.

Tate McRae stays at No. 2 with “Housewife” completing a fourth week atop the songs chart. Jão improves from No. 7 to No. 4, and Olivia Dean makes one of the week's biggest climbs, from No. 41 to No. 10. Grande's position at No. 1 remains unchanged, but the activity behind her shows a ranking in motion—and a new challenger reaching the top three.

artists.title: Ariana Grande Leads the Artist 50 Again as Tame Impala Rises 21 Places and Yseult Debuts
artists.text:
Ariana Grande retains No. 1 on the Daegon Artist 50 dated November 7, extending an exceptionally long presence on the ranking. This is her 474th chart week and her 129th week at the summit, two figures that show how much of her standing has been built over time rather than in a single release cycle.

The current week has its own catalyst: Grande’s petal spends an 11th week at No. 1 on Top 100 Albums, while “hate that i made you love me” holds at No. 2 on the Daegon 100 Songs. Together, those placements help explain why Grande remains ahead of Tate McRae, who is steady at No. 2 on the Artist 50 even as “Housewife” secures a third week atop the songs ranking.

The most striking movement comes further down the top five. Tame Impala jumps from No. 26 to No. 5, the act’s highest Artist 50 placement to date. It is a cross-chart rise: Deadbeat climbs from No. 23 to No. 3 among albums, and “Dracula (with JENNIE)” moves from No. 15 to No. 3 among songs. That combination gives the artist a stronger chart-week narrative than a single isolated leap would suggest.

Olivia Rodrigo also improves, rising from No. 7 to No. 3 as her album moves up to No. 2. Anitta advances from No. 24 to No. 9 alongside the jump of EQUILIBRIVM II, while Yseult makes a first Artist 50 appearance at No. 10 as Freak debuts at No. 7 on the albums chart.

This edition therefore tells two stories at once: Grande’s established longevity at the very top and a reshuffling of the field behind her, with Tame Impala, Rodrigo, Anitta and Yseult driving much of the week’s new movement.
artists.subtitle: Long-running chart leader Grande keeps her crown, but the week’s biggest shake-up belongs to Tame Impala, Anitta and newcomer Yseult.
